title: Identity is computable in linear time
statement: There are a finite Turing machine $M$ over the Boolean alphabet and a constant $c\in\mathbb{N}$ such that, on every Boolean input $x$, $M$ outputs $x$ and halts within $c(|x|+1)$ steps.
replaced:
There exist a multi-tape Turing machine $M$ over the Boolean alphabet and a
constant $c$ such that $M$ computes the identity function on Boolean words in
time $c \cdot (n + 1)$: on every input $x$, within $c \cdot (\abs{x} + 1)$
steps $M$ halts with output exactly $x$.
